corporate-gifting.title: Corporate gifting
corporate-gifting.heading: Thoughtful gifts. Meaningful connections.
corporate-gifting.intro: Plan branded gifts for your team, clients and business milestones. Start with the people receiving them, then choose the contents, packaging and message.
corporate-gifting.advice: Choose practical items people will use beyond the occasion. A consistent colour palette, a useful centrepiece and a personal note can make a modest gift feel considered.
corporate-gifting.planning: Share your recipient count, budget per person, artwork and delivery date. We will confirm available contents, branding options and the final quotation before you place an order.
corporate-gifting.question: Can I include my company logo?
corporate-gifting.answer: Ask about a branded card, sleeve or packaging. The available method and minimum quantity depend on the chosen item.

employee-gifts.title: Employee gifts
employee-gifts.heading: For the people who make it happen.
employee-gifts.intro: Celebrate work anniversaries, achievements and everyday appreciation with employee gift hampers.
employee-gifts.advice: Choose a gift around the moment: desk essentials for a work milestone, a treat-filled box for a team celebration or a handwritten thank-you for individual recognition.
employee-gifts.planning: For a large team, check dietary needs and whether one consistent kit or a choice of options will suit recipients better. Share a delivery plan before confirming your order.
employee-gifts.question: Can gifts include individual names?
employee-gifts.answer: Personalised name cards can be discussed in your quotation. Share the final names and spelling before artwork approval.

client-gifts.title: Client gifts
client-gifts.heading: A thank-you they will remember.
client-gifts.intro: Explore gifting ideas for client appreciation, project handovers and business relationships.
client-gifts.advice: A client gift should reflect the relationship. Consider understated branding, a concise personal message and contents suited to the recipient rather than filling a box with promotional items.
client-gifts.planning: Check your recipient company’s gift policy and any food restrictions before choosing a hamper. Tell us whether gifts go to a single office or several addresses.
client-gifts.question: What should I share for a client-gift quotation?
client-gifts.answer: Include the recipient count, occasion, per-gift budget, preferred contents and delivery locations.

corporate-merchandise.title: Corporate merchandise
corporate-merchandise.heading: Useful objects. Your brand, thoughtfully placed.
corporate-merchandise.intro: Explore logo-ready bottles, tumblers, mugs, keychains, T-shirts and hoodies for teams and events.
corporate-merchandise.advice: Choose useful items your recipients will enjoy: drinkware for desks and commutes, clothing for teams, and small keepsakes for events. Match logo placement and branding method to each material.
corporate-merchandise.planning: Share a clear logo file, garment sizes and preferred colours. Availability, branding technique, sample approval and minimum order quantity must be confirmed before production.
corporate-merchandise.question: Can you reproduce exact brand colours?
corporate-merchandise.answer: We will discuss the closest achievable finish for the chosen material. Approve artwork and any agreed sample before ordering.

employee-welcome-kits.title: Employee welcome gifts
employee-welcome-kits.heading: Welcome them to the team.
employee-welcome-kits.intro: Choose from three illustrated Hamperia welcome-kit options for employee onboarding.
employee-welcome-kits.advice: The Signature, Premium and Essential kits pair branded everyday items with a welcome message. Compare the listed kit images and prices, then share your quantity, artwork and preferred contents.
employee-welcome-kits.planning: Branding, item sizes, final contents, availability and delivery must be confirmed in your quotation. For repeat hiring, ask about ordering the same kit in later batches.
employee-welcome-kits.question: What is included in each welcome kit?
employee-welcome-kits.answer: The supplied images show the proposed items. Check the full image and ask us to confirm your final contents, branding and delivery before ordering.

onboarding-kits.title: Onboarding kits
onboarding-kits.heading: Help them settle in.
onboarding-kits.intro: Pair a welcome gift with practical materials for an employee’s first week.
onboarding-kits.advice: Think beyond the first-day unboxing: a checklist, contact sheet, notebook and welcome message can help a colleague navigate their first week. Avoid printing information that changes frequently.
onboarding-kits.planning: Use a QR code on your own welcome card for internal resources, and keep sensitive employee or company data out of printed gift packaging.
onboarding-kits.question: Can I provide my own onboarding inserts?
onboarding-kits.answer: Yes, discuss insert size, quantity and packing requirements as part of the enquiry; inclusion is confirmed in the quotation.

diwali-gifts.title: Diwali gifts
diwali-gifts.heading: Little lights. Lasting memories.
diwali-gifts.intro: Explore personalised Diwali hamper ideas for family, friends and festive gatherings.
diwali-gifts.advice: Balance a festive centrepiece with contents the recipient enjoys. Consider dry fruits, chocolate or a diya, then bring everything together with a warm note and coordinated wrapping.
diwali-gifts.planning: Before selecting food items, confirm allergies, ingredients and shelf life. Festive availability and delivery dates should be checked before ordering.
diwali-gifts.question: Can I personalise a Diwali hamper?
diwali-gifts.answer: Share your preferred contents, message and colours. We will confirm which customisations are available.

corporate-diwali-gifts.title: Corporate Diwali gifts
corporate-diwali-gifts.heading: Celebrate together, beautifully.
corporate-diwali-gifts.intro: Plan festive hampers for employees, clients and partners with consistent branding and presentation.
corporate-diwali-gifts.advice: Corporate Diwali planning combines recipient lists, budget approval, artwork and delivery windows. Select a small number of hamper options so packing and distribution remain manageable.
corporate-diwali-gifts.planning: Request a quotation with quantity bands and confirm any food restrictions. Approve the contents and message before the festive production schedule fills.
corporate-diwali-gifts.question: When should we start planning?
corporate-diwali-gifts.answer: Start as early as practical and ask for the current production timeline. Your final deadline depends on quantity, customisation and destination.

diwali-gifts-for-employees.title: Diwali gifts for employees
diwali-gifts-for-employees.heading: A festive thank-you to your team.
diwali-gifts-for-employees.intro: Choose inclusive festive gifts that recognise the people behind your business.
diwali-gifts-for-employees.advice: For a varied team, consider shared dietary requirements and packaging that travels well. Offer clear choices only where the packing and fulfilment process can support them.
diwali-gifts-for-employees.planning: Confirm team counts and office distribution dates with HR. Use a consistent message while allowing individual name cards where available.
diwali-gifts-for-employees.question: Can we use different gift options for teams?
diwali-gifts-for-employees.answer: Discuss the number of variants and quantity per variant before finalising the quotation.

diwali-gifts-for-clients.title: Diwali gifts for clients
diwali-gifts-for-clients.heading: Warm wishes, personally delivered.
diwali-gifts-for-clients.intro: Mark the festive season with considered hampers for clients and business partners.
diwali-gifts-for-clients.advice: Choose presentation that feels personal and professional. A short note from the account team is often more meaningful than prominent branding on every item.
diwali-gifts-for-clients.planning: Confirm recipient addresses and gift-policy restrictions. For food hampers, consider transit conditions and the time between packing and delivery.
diwali-gifts-for-clients.question: Can the note be different for each client?
diwali-gifts-for-clients.answer: Ask about variable message cards and provide the final approved text in a consistent list.

gift-hampers.title: Gift hampers

gift-hampers.intro: Discover gift hampers for thoughtful thank-yous, personal celebrations and corporate occasions.
gift-hampers.advice: Choose a theme before selecting individual items. A small, well-matched collection can feel more personal than a larger assortment with no connection.
gift-hampers.planning: Review the contents, packaging and customisation options on each product. Images are presentation inspiration; final details are confirmed before ordering.
gift-hampers.question: Can I swap a hamper item?
gift-hampers.answer: Request the change in your enquiry. Availability and any price difference will be confirmed before ordering.

dry-fruit-hampers.title: Dry fruit hampers
dry-fruit-hampers.heading: A classic, thoughtfully presented.
dry-fruit-hampers.intro: Explore dry-fruit hamper ideas for festive and corporate gifting.
dry-fruit-hampers.advice: Choose sealed portions and a presentation that protects the contents. Clear ingredient information, packing dates and storage instructions matter as much as the box design.
dry-fruit-hampers.planning: Tell us your preferred assortment and recipient restrictions. Nuts are common allergens; confirm the final ingredient list before sharing gifts.
dry-fruit-hampers.question: Can a dry-fruit hamper be nut-free?
dry-fruit-hampers.answer: A nut-free alternative needs a different contents selection. Discuss allergens and cross-contact information before ordering.

chocolate-hampers.title: Chocolate hampers
chocolate-hampers.heading: For the sweeter moments.
chocolate-hampers.intro: Create a chocolate-led gift hamper with a personal card and complementary small gifts.
chocolate-hampers.advice: Use a compact arrangement that protects wrappers and avoids crushing. Match the chocolate selection to recipient preferences and check ingredients where dietary restrictions apply.
chocolate-hampers.planning: Warm-weather transit can affect chocolate. Ask about delivery suitability for the destination and date before confirming the order.
chocolate-hampers.question: Are chocolate hampers suitable for every destination?
chocolate-hampers.answer: Suitability depends on temperature and transit time. Confirm delivery arrangements before ordering.

gourmet-hampers.title: Gourmet hampers
gourmet-hampers.heading: Something delicious to discover.
gourmet-hampers.intro: Plan a food-focused gift around a shared tea break, coffee moment or favourite flavours.
gourmet-hampers.advice: A coherent assortment could pair a beverage with a snack and a small keepsake. Consider serving sizes and whether the gift will be shared by a family or office team.
gourmet-hampers.planning: Ask for the final food list, ingredient details and shelf life. Specific products are subject to sourcing and quotation.
gourmet-hampers.question: Can I choose the food items?
gourmet-hampers.answer: Share preferences and exclusions. We will confirm the available assortment and price.

healthy-hampers.title: Healthy hamper ideas
healthy-hampers.heading: Thoughtful choices for everyday routines.
healthy-hampers.intro: Explore lighter snack and practical gift ideas based on the recipient’s preferences.
healthy-hampers.advice: “Healthy” means different things to different people. Compare actual ingredient and nutrition labels instead of relying on a category name, and ask about added sugar or relevant allergens.
healthy-hampers.planning: These gifts are not dietary or medical advice. Confirm suitability with the recipient and choose products with clear labelling.
healthy-hampers.question: Can you guarantee a specific diet?
healthy-hampers.answer: Do not assume a hamper meets a dietary requirement. Ask for product labels and confirm every item before ordering.

wellness-hampers.title: Wellness hampers
wellness-hampers.heading: A moment to slow down.
wellness-hampers.intro: Build a relaxing gift around a quiet evening, a warm drink or a personal note.
wellness-hampers.advice: Consider a candle, a journal or a beverage as a starting point. Keep fragrance preferences and sensitivities in mind and avoid combining overpowering scents.
wellness-hampers.planning: Check care instructions and safe-use guidance for candles or fragrance products. Contents and availability are confirmed through your enquiry.
wellness-hampers.question: Can I request fragrance-free contents?
wellness-hampers.answer: Mention this in your enquiry so we can discuss suitable alternatives.

posts.title: How to make a gift hamper at home: a thoughtful step-by-step guide
posts.summary: Choose a theme, plan the contents, build a stable arrangement and finish it with a personal message.
takeaways: Choose a recipient and occasion before shopping.
Arrange the contents before you buy the basket or box.
Protect food, glass and scented items for safe presentation and delivery.

sections.heading: 1. Start with the recipient, not the basket
paragraphs: A memorable hamper feels as if it was made for one person. Begin with the occasion and what the recipient enjoys: a quiet tea break, a new home, a birthday, a new job or a festive celebration. That gives you a simple theme to guide every later choice.

Write down one main item and two or three smaller additions that belong with it. For a tea theme, that might mean tea, a snack and a cup. For a new-home gift, consider a useful everyday item with a small treat and a note. A short, coherent list usually looks more considered than a box filled with unrelated things.

sections.heading: 2. Set the budget and check practical details
paragraphs: Decide your total spend before browsing. Include the container, protective filler, ribbon or wrap, message card and delivery materials, as well as the gifts themselves. If you are making several hampers, multiply each per-person cost and keep a little room for breakage or substitutions.

Check food labels, best-before dates, dietary needs and common allergens with care. Keep food sealed and away from candles, fragrance and other scented items. If you do not know the recipient’s restrictions, choose clearly labelled products and avoid making health or dietary promises.

sections.heading: 3. Choose a base that fits the contents
paragraphs: Lay the items out on a table and measure the footprint and tallest item. Then choose a sturdy box, tray or basket that leaves enough room for cushioning without making the contents look lost. A shallow base makes it easier to see each item; a deeper box needs more support so things do not slide.

If the hamper will be carried or shipped, favour a base that can be closed or wrapped securely. Check that the bottom is strong enough for the heaviest item. Glass jars need individual cushioning and should not press against one another.

sections.heading: 4. Build the arrangement before wrapping
paragraphs: Add a layer of filler, then place the heaviest items low and towards the back. Stand taller items behind shorter ones, and turn labels towards the person opening the hamper. Use small pieces of filler to keep items upright and to prevent movement.

Step back and look at the arrangement from the front and from above. Remove anything that blocks another item or makes the hamper feel crowded. Try a simple colour plan, such as kraft and green or cream with one festive accent, and repeat those colours in the card or ribbon.

sections.heading: 5. Add a personal finish and check it can travel
paragraphs: Write a short message that says why you chose the gift. A name tag or a ribbon in a favourite colour can add warmth without adding clutter. Keep the note easy to read and place it where it will be seen first.

Before handing it over, gently tilt the base to check that nothing shifts. Secure the lid or outer wrap, protect fragile corners and add an outer shipping carton if it is travelling. For a larger order, assemble one sample first, photograph the approved arrangement and use it as the packing reference.

posts.title: Gift hamper budget guide: plan the full cost before you buy
posts.summary: A practical way to price the container, gifts, finishing details and delivery without losing sight of the recipient.
takeaways: Set a per-gift ceiling and a total project budget.
Compare complete contents and quantities, not just the headline price.
Get customisation, shipping and delivery terms in the written quote.

sections.heading: Set a per-person target and a total
paragraphs: For a personal gift, choose the total you are comfortable spending. For a team or client order, decide the per-recipient amount and multiply it by the number of gifts. Keep these two figures visible while comparing options so a small upgrade does not quietly change the overall budget.

Reserve part of the total for packaging, a message card, custom branding, shipping and any separate assembly charge. Ask whether the listed price is the finished hamper or an individual component. Hamperia’s supplies are sold as individual items; only products described as hampers are complete combinations.

sections.heading: Price the contents and presentation together
paragraphs: List the main gift, supporting items, base, filler and finishing details. Record the quantity and unit price of each. A neat three-item collection can look more intentional than a larger assortment, and fewer items make it easier to keep the presentation stable.

Compare what is actually included. Check jar count, pack size, item quantity and whether the pictured card or decoration is part of the offer. For a customised order, ask for the final contents and any substitutions to be written into the quote.

sections.heading: Account for branding and quantity
paragraphs: For corporate orders, ask which branding method suits the material: a card, sleeve, tag or printed item may each have different costs and minimum quantities. Share a clear logo file and approve the placement before production. Personalised names can require a separate list and additional checking.

Ask for prices at the quantities you are considering. Some costs change with volume, while individual delivery addresses or different gift variants can add handling work. Confirm the number of each variant rather than relying on an estimated total.

sections.heading: Confirm the final total before you commit
paragraphs: Request one written total that identifies the contents, quantity, customisation, packing, shipping and payment schedule. Confirm the delivery locations and required arrival date. Ask whether taxes or other charges are included instead of assuming they are.

For Hamperia’s listed dry-fruit boxes, the current catalogue shows ₹699 for two glass jars, ₹1,099 for three and ₹1,499 for four. Check the live product page for the final assortment, weights, availability and current terms before ordering.

sections.heading: Keep a simple comparison sheet
paragraphs: A small table helps you compare options fairly: product name, per-gift price, number of pieces, personalisation, delivery, lead time and final total. Add a column for the recipient and occasion so you do not choose on price alone.
If a preferred item may be unavailable, ask for an agreed alternative and its price in advance. That keeps the budget and presentation predictable if a substitution is needed.

posts.title: Corporate gifting guide: plan thoughtful gifts for employees and clients
posts.summary: Compare corporate gift ideas and prepare a clear brief for quantity, budget, branding and delivery.
takeaways: Separate audiences and confirm policies before choosing gifts.
Share quantity, budget, branding and delivery details in one brief.
Approve the final item list and artwork before production.

sections.heading: 1. Define the purpose and recipients
paragraphs: Start by writing down what the gift should communicate: welcome a new colleague, thank a client, recognise a milestone or mark a festive occasion. The purpose helps you choose between practical merchandise, a food-led hamper or a small keepsake with a personal message.

Separate employee, client and partner recipients when their preferences, policies or delivery plans differ. Check any company rules about gifts, value limits or food before selecting items. For food gifts, plan how ingredient and allergen information will be shared.

sections.heading: 2. Prepare a complete enquiry brief
paragraphs: Include the occasion, recipient count, budget per person, total budget, preferred items, required date and delivery locations. Add whether you want branded packaging, logo-ready merchandise, individual name cards or a consistent note. This information makes a quotation easier to understand and compare.

For apparel, estimate sizes and colours. For drinkware and merchandise, provide the logo artwork and any placement preferences. If you do not yet know every address, share the likely number of destinations and confirm when the final list will be ready.

sections.heading: 3. Choose the right kind of gift
paragraphs: A useful workday item such as a notebook or bottle can suit onboarding and team recognition. A curated hamper can mark a celebration or client milestone. A combination of branded merchandise and a small treat may work well for an event, provided the packaging can protect every item.

Keep the range manageable. Too many choices can make approvals, packing and distribution harder. If you need different gifts for different recipient groups, state each group’s quantity and budget clearly.

sections.heading: 4. Review contents, artwork and price
paragraphs: Check the full contents list, quantities and final product images. Ask which branding method is available for each material and request a proof for approval. Review names, spelling, dates, logo proportions and message text before signing off.

Ask for a complete quote that shows the gifts, packaging, branding, assembly, delivery and payment terms. Confirm whether prices are final and whether shipping or other charges are included. Hamperia product pages describe the current listed options; customised corporate work is confirmed by quotation.

sections.heading: 5. Plan fulfilment and keep a record
paragraphs: Confirm who will receive the shipment, how many parcels are expected and when the gifts need to arrive. For multiple addresses, agree a secure process for sharing recipient details. Leave time for production, packing and a check of quantities before the event.

Keep the approved contents, artwork, quote and delivery plan together. If a product must be substituted, confirm the replacement and any price change before it is packed. After delivery, reconcile the quantity received with the approved order.

posts.title: Corporate Diwali gifts: a practical guide to planning a thoughtful order
posts.summary: Compare festive hamper options, prepare your recipient list and confirm customisation and delivery before the season gets busy.
takeaways: Plan recipients, quantities and delivery destinations first.
Compare the complete contents and food information for each option.
Approve the message, branding and written quotation before production.

sections.heading: Start with the people receiving the gift
paragraphs: Make separate lists for employees, clients and business partners if their gift policies, budgets or delivery needs differ. Confirm how many people are included, whether gifts will go to one office or many addresses, and when each group needs to receive them.

For food gifts, ask about ingredient information and common allergens before selecting the assortment. A festive theme can still feel inclusive when the contents are clearly described and the message is warm without making assumptions about how each person celebrates.

sections.heading: Compare contents, presentation and budget
paragraphs: Hamperia’s current Diwali catalogue includes listed hamper options at ₹1,499, ₹2,499 and ₹3,499. The product descriptions show different combinations of dry fruits, chocolates, a candle, a diffuser, decorative idols and a greeting card. Read the live product page for the exact proposed contents and confirm item quantities, food labels and presentation in your quotation.

Compare the complete set rather than the headline price alone. Ask whether the gift box, message card, logo treatment, assembly and delivery are included. If you are considering several price points, make sure each option has a clear contents list so recipients receive what was approved.

sections.heading: Make personalisation easy to approve
paragraphs: Prepare a high-quality logo file, the greeting text and any names that need to appear on individual cards. Decide where branding should appear and whether you prefer a subtle tag, sleeve or printed element. The available method depends on the chosen product and packaging.

Ask for a digital artwork proof and check spelling, colour, logo size and safe margins. Confirm any sample represents the final materials and finish. Keep the approved version with the order so it can be used as the reference during packing.

sections.heading: Build a realistic delivery schedule
paragraphs: Share the quantity, delivery locations and required arrival date when requesting a quote. Ask for the current production estimate and the last date for approving artwork. Multiple destinations, custom branding and different hamper variants can affect the schedule, so confirm a plan for each shipment.

Before final approval, request one written quote that lists contents, quantities, packaging, personalisation, delivery and payment terms. Confirm how substitutions will be handled if a product becomes unavailable. A clear record makes it easier for your team to approve the order and check what arrives.

posts.title: Employee welcome kit checklist: what new joiners will actually use
posts.summary: Choose practical first-day essentials, plan personalisation and make repeat onboarding orders easier to manage.
takeaways: Start with useful items and a concise welcome message.
Collect sizes and names only after deciding what needs personalisation.
Record the approved kit so future batches stay consistent.

sections.heading: Choose essentials for the first week
paragraphs: A good welcome kit supports the first days at work. A notebook, pen and water bottle are straightforward starting points; a tumbler or branded clothing can add value when employees are likely to use them. Keep the kit relevant to the work and avoid adding items simply to increase the piece count.

A short card from the team can make the welcome feel personal. Keep operational instructions and confidential company information in internal onboarding materials that can be updated, rather than printing details that may change on the gift packaging.

sections.heading: Compare the Hamperia welcome-kit options
paragraphs: Hamperia currently lists an Essential kit at ₹999 with a bottle, notebook and pen; a Premium kit at ₹1,899 with a bottle, notebook, pen and tumbler; and a Signature kit at ₹2,999 that also includes a T-shirt, keychain and personalised message card. Confirm the live product listing for current contents, colours and availability before ordering.

For a large intake, decide whether everyone receives one standard kit or whether roles or locations need different versions. A consistent kit is simpler to pack and replenish. If you choose variants, make a clear count for every option and include that breakdown in the quotation request.

sections.heading: Gather branding details and sizes
paragraphs: Share the logo file, preferred placement and any brand-colour guidance. Ask which branding methods are suitable for each item; print quality and colour can vary by material. Review artwork proofs before approval and check that the logo remains legible at the proposed size.

If a kit includes clothing, decide how sizes will be collected and who will check them. For individual message cards, use a final spreadsheet with one spelling source and review a proof before production. Do not send personal employee data through an unagreed channel.

sections.heading: Plan packing, delivery and future batches
paragraphs: Confirm the hire date, recipient count, office locations and whether the kits should arrive before or on the first day. Ask about current stock and production time, especially if you expect new joiners throughout the year. A small buffer helps when start dates change.

Keep the approved contents, artwork and quote together as a repeat-order record. Before each later batch, reconfirm item availability, prices, sizes and branding. The product images illustrate the proposed presentation; ask for final contents and packing details to be confirmed in writing.

posts.title: How to plan a bulk gift order for employees or clients
posts.summary: Use a clear brief and a simple approval checklist to compare quantities, branding, packaging and delivery plans.
takeaways: Put recipient count, budget and required date in one brief.
Compare complete quotes and quantities across suppliers.
Approve the final item list, artwork and delivery plan in writing.

sections.heading: Write a brief before requesting prices
paragraphs: State the occasion, recipient count, budget per gift, total budget and required arrival date. Note whether you need a ready-made hamper, branded merchandise or individual components to assemble yourself. Add delivery locations and any dietary or packaging requirements so suppliers can quote for the real scope.

Identify who approves the budget, artwork and final contents. If more than one team is involved, set a date for each approval. This avoids choosing a product before the people who need to sign off have seen the details.

sections.heading: Make options easy to compare
paragraphs: Ask each supplier to list the exact items and quantities, packaging, branding method, unit price, shipping and payment terms. Compare like with like: a gift with a printed message or individual delivery may not be comparable to a standard boxed product.

Limit the number of variants unless recipient needs justify them. If you do need separate employee and client gifts, show the quantity and budget for each group. For apparel, include estimated sizes; for drinkware and merchandise, share the preferred logo placement and colours.

sections.heading: Review samples and artwork carefully
paragraphs: Ask what a sample includes and whether it uses the final materials, print method and packaging. Check that food labels, product quantities and any included card are represented accurately. For digital artwork, review names, spelling, dates, logo proportions and colour before signing off.

Record approved changes. If a chosen item may be replaced, agree what substitutions are acceptable and whether they affect price. The final order should match the written approval rather than relying on a message or an illustrative image alone.

sections.heading: Plan distribution and close the loop
paragraphs: Decide whether the order will be delivered to one office or packed for individual destinations. Agree how recipient addresses will be shared and when the final list is due. Ask for a realistic production and delivery estimate that accounts for branding, assembly and destination count.

When the order arrives, check the number of packages and compare the contents with the approved list. Keep the quotation, artwork proof and delivery record together; these details make a repeat order much easier to run.

posts.title: How to choose a dry fruit gift box: jars, assortment and presentation
posts.summary: Compare jar counts, check food details and choose packaging that suits a personal or corporate gift.
takeaways: Choose a jar count that fits the occasion and recipient.
Ask for net weight, assortment, ingredients and storage details.
Confirm packaging and delivery for the actual destination.

sections.heading: Choose the size for the occasion
paragraphs: Jar count is a useful first comparison, but it does not tell the whole story. Consider how many people will share the gift, whether it is a small thank-you or a larger festive gesture, and how the recipient will store it. A compact box may be easier to distribute to a team, while a larger assortment can suit a family or a more significant occasion.

Hamperia’s current catalogue lists a two-glass-jar box at ₹699, a three-jar box at ₹1,099 and a four-jar box at ₹1,499. Check the live listing and ask for the selected assortment, jar capacity, net weights and availability before placing an order.

sections.heading: Look beyond the jar count
paragraphs: Ask which dry fruits are included, whether the selection is fixed and how each item is packed. The number of jars does not indicate the quantity of food inside each jar. Clear net-weight information helps you compare options fairly and tell recipients what they are receiving.

Check the ingredient list, packing date, best-before information and storage instructions. Nuts are common allergens. If you are buying for a group, confirm whether the products may be packed or handled alongside other allergens and share accurate product information with recipients.

sections.heading: Choose a box that protects the contents
paragraphs: Glass jars need a box insert or cushioning that prevents them from knocking together during handling. Ask how the box will be packed and whether it is suitable for courier delivery to your destination. For a corporate event, confirm how many boxes fit in an outer carton and how the labels will be protected.

A coordinated ribbon or message card can personalise the gift without obscuring product labels. If adding custom branding, approve a proof and confirm whether it changes the packaging, minimum quantity or delivery schedule.

sections.heading: Confirm food and delivery details before ordering
paragraphs: Request a written contents list, final price and delivery estimate. Confirm whether the listed amount includes the gift box, personalisation and shipping. For a bulk order, give the recipient count and destination breakdown so packing and transport can be planned accurately.

Food contents and sourcing can change. Treat catalogue images as presentation references and confirm the exact assortment and labels for your order. Do not describe the gift as suitable for a dietary requirement unless every included product and its handling information has been checked.

posts.title: Corporate merchandise guide: choose branded gifts people will use
posts.summary: Plan branded bottles, tumblers, mugs, apparel and keepsakes with the right artwork, quantity and approval process.
takeaways: Match the item to how recipients will use it.
Check artwork, material, size and minimum quantities before approval.
Ask for the branded sample or proof and confirm the delivery plan.

sections.heading: Start with the use, then choose the item
paragraphs: Useful branded gifts begin with the recipient’s routine. Bottles and tumblers can suit commuting or desk use; mugs can work for an office or event; notebooks and pens are practical for training; keychains are compact event keepsakes. T-shirts and hoodies need more planning because fit, fabric, size and colour all matter.

Choose one or two items that serve the occasion instead of applying a logo to everything. Think about whether the gift will be used at a workplace, taken home or carried while travelling. That context can guide the item, size and packaging.

sections.heading: Prepare artwork that works on the material
paragraphs: Provide a clear vector logo or a high-resolution file and specify any brand-colour requirements. Ask how the design will be applied to each surface and where it will sit. A detailed logo may need a simplified treatment on a small keychain, while a garment may need a larger print area.

Review a digital proof for size, position, colour and legibility. If the finish or material is important, ask whether a physical sample is available and whether it reflects the production method. Approve only after the intended design is clear.

sections.heading: Plan quantities, variants and sizing
paragraphs: Share the quantity per item and the number of colour or design variants. Minimum quantities can differ by product and branding method, so ask for the threshold and unit price at your expected volume. Different options for each department may be useful, but too many variants can complicate packing and distribution.

For T-shirts and hoodies, estimate sizes early and decide how employees will select them. Ask how size exchanges or extra units are handled. For drinkware, confirm capacity, material, care instructions and whether the item is suitable for the use you have in mind.

sections.heading: Compare a complete quote and delivery plan
paragraphs: Ask the supplier to specify the product, material, branding, packaging, quantity, unit price, delivery charge and payment schedule. Confirm whether setup or artwork charges apply and whether the amount includes taxes. For a mixed merchandise kit, check the cost and packing plan for the complete set.

Before production, approve the proof, quantity breakdown and delivery date in writing. If the gifts are for an event, leave time for a sample review and an arrival check. Hamperia can discuss logo-ready bottles, tumblers, mugs, keychains, T-shirts and hoodies; final availability, branding and price are confirmed in the quote.

posts.title: How to choose a personalised gift hamper for any occasion
posts.summary: A simple guide to matching the recipient, occasion, contents and message without making the gift feel generic.
takeaways: Let the recipient and occasion shape the theme.
Check contents and practical needs before choosing presentation.
Use one personal detail to make the gift feel considered.

sections.heading: Think about who will receive it
paragraphs: A useful gift starts with the person, not a trend. Consider their interests, daily routine, the relationship you share and whether the gift is for one person or a household. A tea-time collection, a small desk set or a festive assortment can each make sense for a different recipient.

If you are unsure about personal preferences, choose versatile items and keep the message thoughtful. For food, check for allergies and dietary needs; for fragrance, consider sensitivities; for clothing, confirm size and style before ordering.

sections.heading: Match the presentation to the moment
paragraphs: A birthday, new job, housewarming and client thank-you call for different tones. A handwritten card can make a simple gift feel personal, while coordinated packaging can make a team order feel polished. Choose colours and decoration that support the gift rather than compete with it.

For a corporate gift, keep branding clear and appropriate to the relationship. A logo on a message card or sleeve can be enough. For a personal gift, a name, short note or favourite colour may feel more meaningful than extra branded objects.

sections.heading: Check the details before you decide
paragraphs: Read the product description and contents list. Confirm the number and size of items, what is included in the box and what the image is intended to illustrate. Check ingredients and storage information for food, care details for candles or fragrance, and sizes for apparel.

Set a budget that includes packaging and delivery. If you want substitutions or customisation, ask what is possible and request the final arrangement and price in writing before payment. Availability and presentation can vary, so use the confirmed order details as the source of truth.

sections.heading: Add one detail that makes it yours
paragraphs: Choose one clear personal touch: a message written for the occasion, a name tag, or a small item connected to a shared memory. A concise note in your own words often has more impact than a long generic greeting.

For bulk gifts, personalisation can be planned with a master message and a verified recipient list. Confirm the spelling and the method for sharing names before the artwork is approved. Browse Hamperia’s ready-made hampers or use the store to create a custom hamper brief from individual components.

posts.title: Diwali gifting guide: how to choose a hamper for family, employees or clients
posts.summary: Compare Diwali hamper contents, presentation and delivery needs to find a festive gift that suits its recipient.
takeaways: Choose a gift around the recipient and the relationship.
Check food contents, labels, packaging and delivery suitability.
For company orders, plan quantities and branding before the festive rush.

sections.heading: Choose the right Diwali gift for the recipient
paragraphs: A Diwali gift for family can be personal and relaxed; an employee gift should feel inclusive across the team; and a client hamper often benefits from a concise note and understated branding. Start with who will receive it, what you want the gift to communicate and whether it will be shared.

Set a budget for each recipient before choosing the assortment. If you are buying for a group, confirm the number of gifts and whether any recipients need a different option. A clear plan makes it easier to compare festive hampers and avoid last-minute changes.

sections.heading: Compare what is inside each hamper
paragraphs: Look at the actual contents and quantities, not only the box or festive artwork. Hamperia’s current Diwali listings show options at ₹1,499, ₹2,499 and ₹3,499 with differing combinations of dry fruits, chocolates, a candle, a diffuser, decorative idols and a greeting card. Read each live product description and confirm the final assortment, jar sizes or quantities, and current price before ordering.

If the gift includes food, request ingredient, allergen, packing-date and storage information. Do not assume a product is suitable for a particular diet unless every item and its handling details have been checked. If an item is unavailable, agree on any replacement and price before it is packed.

sections.heading: Make the presentation festive and practical
paragraphs: A coordinated box, ribbon and greeting card can create a festive first impression. The contents should remain the focus: choose a colour palette that complements the gifts, and leave labels visible where recipients need food or care information.

Think about how the hamper will be carried or delivered. Jars and fragile decorations need protection; candles and fragrance items should be secured and separated from food. Ask how the packaging is prepared for transport to the actual destination.

sections.heading: Plan corporate and bulk Diwali gifting early
paragraphs: For employee and client gifts, prepare the recipient count, delivery list, budget per gift, logo artwork and message before requesting a quote. Ask about branding choices, order quantities, production time and delivery dates. If there are multiple offices or addresses, describe the distribution plan so fulfilment can be estimated accurately.

Review a written quotation with the complete contents, customisation, packing and delivery charges. Approve the message and artwork carefully, then keep the final version with your order. Start early enough to review a sample and allow time for packing and delivery before your celebration.
